source_text: Welcome to the annual security awareness module for GMO employees in India.
This module takes about eight minutes and ends with five questions.
Most breaches begin with one person clicking one link.
Phishing is an email that tries to make you act before you think.
It will claim something is urgent: an expiring password, a blocked payment, a missed delivery.
Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for all systems that hold client data.
MFA means a password alone is never enough to reach client data.
Attackers know this, so they now target the second factor as well.
If an OTP arrives that you did not request, someone already has your password.
Do not approve it, and change that password from a device you trust.
Report any suspected phishing email to the security team within 24 hours.
Twenty-four hours matters because attackers move laterally within a day.
A common local variant is a UPI payment request that looks like a refund.
A refund never requires you to approve a payment or enter your PIN.
Vishing is the same trick over a phone call, often from a spoofed helpdesk number.
Our helpdesk will never ask for your password or an OTP on a call.
Do not share your VPN credentials with anyone, including IT staff.
Use the password manager rather than a spreadsheet or a note on your laptop.
Violations may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination.
If you are unsure whether a message is genuine, forward it and ask. Nobody is penalised for checking.
